intended_object: An identity linear equivalence (`LinearEquiv.refl`) between the carrier of the finite-projective product `pi Ri Mi` and the module `ModuleCat.piRight Ri (fun i => (Mi i).obj)`. The two are definitionally the same module. This is clear from the body and from the docstring ("by the identity on functions").
explanation: The body is `LinearEquiv.refl` on `ModuleCat.piRight Ri (fun i => (Mi i).obj)`. Its only job is to move between two definitionally equal presentations of the same module: the carrier of the bundled finite-projective product and the plain coefficient-product module. Its simp lemmas `piLinearEquiv_apply` and `piLinearEquiv_symm_apply` are both proved by `rfl`. The library uses it only as a rewriting tool, for example in `pi_eq_finsum_single`. It does not define any mathematical construction of its own, so it is an implementation device and has no literature counterpart to compare it with.
